prompt: Bug report from a user: "Track files exported from my Garmin app fail with `trailhead: line 1: expected the header 'lat,lon,ele'`, but when I open one in my editor the first line is exactly `lat,lon,ele`. One of the files is attached as `garmin-export.csv`." Find the cause and fix it.
bash_commands: git ls-files; head -c 64 garmin-export.csv | xxd | head -5; grep -rn "expected the header" --include=* . 2>/dev/null | grep -v '^./.git/' | head
cat -A garmin-export.csv | tail -5; cat src/trailhead/track.py; grep -rn "open(\|read_text\|encoding" src tests | grep -v "track.py"

python - <<'EOF'
import re,pathlib
p=pathlib.Path("src/trailhead/track.py"); s=p.read_text()
s=s.replace('''    header_seen = False
    for number, raw in enumerate(text.splitlines(), start=1):''','''    header_seen = False
    # Some exporters (e.g. Garmin) start the file with a UTF-8 byte order mark.
    text = text.removeprefix("\\ufeff")
    for number, raw in enumerate(text.splitlines(), start=1):''')
p.write_text(s)
EOF
grep -n "def test\|^import\|^from" tests/test_track.py | head -30; sed -n 1,40p tests/conftest.py

cat >> tests/test_track.py <<'EOF'


def test_byte_order_mark_and_crlf_are_accepted(write_track):
    path = write_track("﻿lat,lon,ele\r\n42.2031,23.3205,2140\r\n42.2049,23.3188,2196\r\n")
    track = load_track(path)
    assert [point.ele for point in track.points] == [2140.0, 2196.0]
EOF
python -m pytest -q 2>&1 | tail -3; PYTHONPATH=src python -m trailhead --help | head -20
